item.title: Latin Fridays & Saturdays at Lula Lounge — Sat Sep 5, 8:00 PM — Lula Lounge
item.description:
Weekends, we go to Havana, where the vibrant rhythms ignite our souls and live music, dance lessons, & skillful DJs make it a perfect night!
Arrive between 7pm and 8pm to indulge in a delectable three-course dinner and explore the Lula carefully curated bar menu, featuring our signature tropical cocktails. The dance lesson at 9pm will ease you into the Latin groove, preparing you for a night of dancing to the tropical rhythms of one of Lula’s world-famous live salsa orchestras, performing two sets starting at 10pm and midnight. Between live music sets, Lula’s talented DJs keep the party going with a mix of top 40, salsa, bachata, reggaeton, and other Latin hits. Don’t miss out on this electrifying night! Agenda 7:00 PM Doors Open for Dinner and Drinks Arrive between 7 and 8 pm to enjoy a fabulous dinner and tropical drinks. item.title: 2026 Philosophy Undergraduate Orientation and Welcome Event — Fri Sep 11, 1:00 PM — Jackman Humanities Building 100
item.description:
Philosophy Undergraduates, comes join us for an introduction to the Department of Philosophy at U of T’s St. George campus. Highlights of the event include -Words of welcome and brief overview of the program from Mike Miller, the Undergraduate Chair -A quick survey of the department’s offerings with Profs. Monica Ding, Andrew Franklin-Hall, Stephen Menn and David Rattray -Introductions from members of the Philosophy Course Union (PCU), the department’s undergraduate student association, giving a sneak peek of events in the year to come -Information about other philosophy student groups like Philosophers for Humanity and Noesis (UofT’s Undergraduate Journal of Philosophy) -And an introduction session about the PHL1 program A short reception will follow where you’ll have a chance to meet some of the faculty and your fellow undergraduates! Come with all your questions! If you are interested in attending, please RSVP here: 2026 Orientation RSVP
Source: UofT Philosophy

item.title: Community Plant Swap at the Liberty Village Eco-Fair — Sat Sep 12, 4:30 PM — Liberty Village Park
item.description:
Toronto plant lovers are invited to a free neighbourhood plant exchange for seasoned growers, curious beginners and anyone ready to take home something green. Bring healthy, pest-free potted plants, plant babies, rooted cuttings, herbs, succulents or cacti. Registration opens at 4:30 p.m. and the plant swap runs from 5 to 6 p.m. Participants receive one swap ticket for each eligible plant they bring. No plant? You can still come meet local plant people and browse, though availability for non-swappers is not guaranteed. RSVP encouraged and walk-ins welcome. Part of the free Liberty Village Eco-Fair.

item.title: Warren Senders: Entering the World of Raga — Sat Sep 19, 7:30 PM — Aga Khan Museum
item.description:
Enjoy an evening of soulful vocals, intricate rhythms, and musical exchange at the Aga Khan Museum.
Bringing together three accomplished artists of classical music, this vocal recital celebrates the expressive depth of raga through voice, harmonium, and tabla. Acclaimed khayal vocalist Warren brings decades of experience with Indian, Western, African, and African-American music. He is joined by harmonium accompanist Hardeep and distinguished tabla artist Kiran.
Together, the musicians create an intimate and dynamic musical exchange, balancing the meditative qualities of raga with the energy of rhythmic interplay and improvisation.

item.title: L'univers sombre et magnifique — Sat Sep 26, 11:00 AM — North York Central Library
item.description: Depuis des millénaires, les êtres humains contemplent le ciel nocturne et s'interrogent sur l'origine de l'univers. D'où vient-il ? De quoi est-ce fait? Où va-t-il? Dans cette présentation, Renée Hložek vous parlerai de cet univers — à la fois sombre et magnifique — et de la manière dont nous utilisons les télescopes pour en percer les secrets. Renée Hložek est cosmologiste sud-africaine et professeure agrégée au Dunlap Institute for Astronomy & Astrophysics de l’Université de Toronto. Ses recherches portent sur les origines et l’évolution de l’Univers, notamment le fond diffus cosmologique, l’énergie noire et la matière noire. Elle participe à d’importantes collaborations internationales, telles que l’Atacama Cosmology Telescope, le Simons Observatory et le Vera C. Rubin Observatory. Elle a reçu la médaille du roi Charles III pour la communication d’idées scientifiques, ainsi que la médaille Rutherford et la bourse Arthur B.
